Jordan (Design): Quick sync — we need to lock the form validation & destructive-confirm patterns for Console v2 before next sprint. Figured a short thread first. https://www.figma.com/file/abcd/form-patterns :point_right: Priya S: +1. Can we explicitly call out accessibility requirements in the pattern doc? screen readers struggle when errors are only visual. :wheelchair: Alex H: For me, inline errors on blur are way better UX. Users fix immediate fields instead of hunting a top banner. reduces time to correction. :rocket: Sam B: Inline errors are good but two caveats: layout shift when messages appear, and long forms where errors below-the-fold get missed unless we scroll. We should reserve space or anchor the input container. :thinking_face: Chris M: Required markers — are we ok with asterisks only? asterisk + legend vs explicit "Required" label per field? I'm leaning towards asterisk + accessible hint for compactness. :star: Priya S: Asterisk only is ambiguous for assistive tech. Recommend: asterisk visually, plus `aria-required="true"` on inputs and a visible legend at the top: "* Required fields". Also ensure error text uses `role="alert"` or `aria-live="assertive"`. Small code snippet: ```
Please enter a valid email
``` Alex H: That snippet looks good. For timing: validate on blur and again on submit. On submit, we show a compact top summary with anchors to each errored field. That satisfies both inline feedback and global discoverability. :white_check_mark: Sam B: Agree on the two-level approach (inline + summary). For layout shift, we can reserve a 24px area under fields for potential error copy or use absolute-positioned error overlays that don't push layout. Also note mobile — reserved space is better there. Jordan (Design): Nice — consensus forming. Now destructive actions: modal confirmation vs undo toast. Thoughts? Example: deleting a Dedicated pool vs removing a single routing rule. Chris M: Tiered approach: low-impact (single item) -> immediate delete with undo toast. High-impact (resource with billing/SLA implications) -> blocking modal that requires typing the resource name or checking "I understand". The typed-name prevents accidental clicks. Alex H: Totally. We did typed-confirm on a previous product and it reduced mistakes. But for any modal, surface the consequences clearly (what is deleted, downstream effects). Also add a small inline link to rollback docs. Priya S: From a11y POV, avoid traps: if modal appears, focus must move to it, and Escape should close only if action isn't destructive (or it should explicitly require dismiss control). For typed confirmations, include `aria-describedby` for instructions. designbot: automated-a11y-bot results: latest-run 2026-03-18 — inline-error role=alert pattern passes contrast & screen-reader detection in 87% of sample pages; top-summary anchors need `aria-invalid` propagation in 2 pages. See /ci/reports/1234. :robot_face: Jordan (Design): Ok proposed pattern to ship in spec: - Field-level: inline error on blur + `aria-live`/`role=alert`, reserve space to avoid shift. - Submit-level: error summary banner with links to fields, focus moves to banner on submit if errors exist. - Required: asterisk + legend + `aria-required` on inputs. - Destructive: tiered confirmations: undo toast for low-risk; modal + typed-name or checkbox for high-risk. Can we call this decision and get owners? Sam B: I'll prototype reserved-space CSS and mobile behavior. Assign to me. Alex H: I'll add the code examples to the component library and a short Storybook demo of the summary banner linking to fields. Priya S: I'll write the accessibility checklist and examples for the doc, including focus management and ARIA attributes. Jordan (Design): I'll update the Figma components + create final spec doc with examples and screenshots. Target: PR by Thu EOD. :calendar: Chris M: I'll surface any edge cases from backend validation (e.g., multi-field errors) and ensure our error payload supports field anchors. Jordan (Design): Sweet. If nobody objects, I'll mark this as the pattern we adopt and update RFC. :thumbsup: Alex H: :thumbsup: Priya S: :+1: Sam B: :thumbsup: Chris M: :+1: designbot: scheduled-reminder set for 1767580000 to check PRs and a11y-run results.
